key_insight: Local atomic-swap tests indicate that GNN feature rankings can reflect physically meaningful neighbor-shell effects even in deliberately overfit models.
engineering_relevance: Perturbation-based validation can help engineers assess whether materials-model explanations capture local chemistry rather than global composition artifacts.
method: Train a deliberately overfit, physics-aware GNN ensemble on DFT-derived CoMoFeNiCu decomposition enthalpies.
Constrain output weights to encode feature importance.
Swap individual atomic sites and re-rank features to test spatial sensitivity.
evidence_signal: Across three stoichiometries and approximately 900 binary and 4,500 ternary decomposition pathways, attribution changes showed spatial decay consistent with the GNN interaction cutoff.
watch_item: Interpretability validation in this limited, deliberately overfit setting does not establish predictive generalization to new compositions or chemistries.
paper_title: Validating Graph Neural Network Feature Attribution Through Local Perturbations: A Study on CoMoFeNiCu Decomposition Enthalpy
